mainTopic: How much of an animal must be inside the פסי ביראות when it drinks or is fed, and for whom the פסי ביראות leniency was made
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא saying that a person drinking from another domain needs his ראשו ורובו (head and most of his body) inside, and that the same is true in a גת. It then asks whether a cow drinking at the פסי ביראות also needs ראשה ורובה inside, and splits the question by whether he holds only the bucket or also the cow. Proofs from our משנה are rejected, along with a ברייתא forbidding holding water before one's animal. אביי explains that ברייתא as a special גזירה about a manger reaching into the רשות הרבים. After a challenge from רבי יוחנן's rule, the גמרא changes the reason for that גזירה to the worry that he will carry the bucket back in. The whole discussion is then retold in a second version (איכא דאמרי), where the easy and doubtful cases are switched. Next, ברייתות about force-feeding a camel or animal are brought as proofs. רב ששת answers that a camel is different because of its long neck, and a ברייתא of רבי אלעזר supports him. Finally, רבי יצחק בר אדא says פסי ביראות were permitted only for עולי רגלים, which is reconciled with a ברייתא that says 'animals'. The rule for a person continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The same rule applies in a winepress
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that the 'head and most of the body' rule also applies to drinking in a גת (winepress).
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true in a winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words are the last line of a ברייתא that was quoted on the previous amud. That ברייתא said a person drinking from another area must put his ראשו ורובו into the place he drinks from. These words add that the same rule applies to drinking wine in a גת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a גת, the grapes are not yet fully processed, so a person may drink casually (שתיית עראי) without first separating מעשר. That counts as casual drinking only if his ראשו ורובו is inside the גת while he drinks. So the 'head and most of the body' standard is used here for a second, separate area of הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Winepress, where grapes are pressed into wine
And likewise; the same rule applies
Tithe; the portion that must be separated from produce before eating it normally

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not start a new topic. It is the closing words of the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud, which required a person's ראשו ורובו to be in the place he drinks from.

phrases.english: And likewise in a winepress.
phrases.notes: Drinking in the winepress counts as casual drinking that is exempt from מעשר only if his head and most of his body are inside the winepress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud by applying its rule to a winepress.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a גת too, a person counts as drinking there only if his ראשו ורובו is inside.

steps.title: Does a cow also need its head and most of its body inside?
steps.stepSummary: Since a person needs ראשו ורובו inside, the גמרא asks whether a cow drinking from the well needs ראשה ורובה inside too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a person, it was said that his head and most of his body must be inside. For a cow, do we need its head and most of its body inside, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question (a בעיא). It already knows the rule for a person, and now asks whether the same rule applies to a cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for a person is clear from the ברייתא. A cow drinking is different, because the cow itself cannot break שבת. The doubt is whether we still demand that its ראשה ורובה be inside the enclosure around the well.

keyTerms.meaning: His head and most of his body

phrases.english: Regarding a person,
it was said that his head and most of his body are required.
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Regarding a cow,
do we require its head and most of its body to be inside
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּי פָּרָה מִי בָּעִינַן לַהּ רֹאשָׁהּ וְרוּבָּהּ אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule for a person and asks whether it also applies to an animal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a drinking cow must have ראשה ורובה inside the enclosure around the well.

steps.title: Narrowing the question to holding both bucket and cow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that if he holds only the bucket, the cow certainly needs ראשה ורובה inside. The real question is when he holds both the bucket and the cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whenever he holds the bucket but does not hold the cow, there is no question: its head and most of its body must be inside. Your question is where he holds the bucket and also holds the cow. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refines its own question. It sets aside the easy case and points to the case that is really in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he holds only the bucket, the cow might back out and pull the bucket with it. He would then end up carrying the bucket from one domain to another, so ראשה ורובה must be inside. If he also holds the cow, he can stop it from backing out, so maybe the requirement is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel; here, the bucket the cow drinks from
Do not ask about this; it is obvious

steps.whyThisMatters: This narrowing tells us exactly which case the proof in the next step has to address.

phrases.english: Wherever he holds the bucket
but does not hold the cow,
there is no question for you
that its head and most of its body must be inside.
phrases.notes: Otherwise the cow might pull the bucket out with it.

phrases.english: Where you should ask

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּנָקֵיט מָנָא וְנָקֵיט לַהּ, מַאי?
phrases.english: is where he holds the bucket and also holds the cow. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּקָא נָקֵיט מָנָא וְלָא נָקֵיט לַהּ לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from step 2 down to the case that is really in doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ראשה ורובה must be inside when he holds both the bucket and the cow.

steps.title: Attempted proof from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: Someone answers from the משנה, which requires the enclosure to fit a cow's ראשה ורובה, and suggests it refers even to a case where he holds both the cow and the bucket.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it: 'As long as the cow has its head and most of its body inside and drinks.' Does this not mean even where he holds the cow and holds the bucket?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone tries to answer the question using the words of our משנה about פסי ביראות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires ראשה ורובה inside, and it does not say whether he is holding the cow. The proof assumes the משנה covers every case, including one where he holds both. If so, ראשה ורובה is required even then.

keyTerms.meaning: You have already learned it (in a משנה)
As long as; on condition that
Is it not? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: He said to him: You already learned it:
as long as the cow is
with its head and most of its body inside, and drinks.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה about the boards around a well.

phrases.english: Is it not referring
to a case where he holds the cow and holds the bucket?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the narrowed question from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That ראשה ורובה is required even when he holds both the cow and the bucket.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: ובלבד שתהא הפרה ראשה ורובה מבפנים ושותה.

steps.title: Rejection: the משנה may be about holding only the bucket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה may be speaking only about a case where he holds the bucket but not the cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is about where he holds the bucket but does not hold the cow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from step 4 and shows that the משנה can be read another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה may be describing only the easy case from step 3, where the cow could pull the bucket out. If so, the משנה tells us nothing about holding both, and the question stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: If he holds only the bucket, the cow must have ראשה ורובה inside. The case where he holds both the bucket and the cow is still unresolved, because the משנה can be read as referring only to the bucket-only case.

phrases.english: No,
it refers to where he holds the bucket but does not hold the cow.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא דְּנָקֵיט מָנָא וְלָא נָקֵיט לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. The question itself is left open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה covers every case, but it can be read as referring only to where he holds the bucket and not the cow.

steps.title: Is holding only the bucket even allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 5. A ברייתא says a person may not fill water and hold it in front of his animal on שבת. He may only pour it out so the animal drinks by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he holds the bucket but does not hold the cow, is that even allowed? But a ברייתא taught: A person may not fill water and put it in front of his animal on שבת. But he may fill it and pour it out, and the animal drinks on its own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 5. It shows a ברייתא that seems to forbid exactly the case Step 5 used: holding the bucket without holding the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the משנה is talking about someone who holds the bucket but not the cow, and that this is permitted. But the ברייתא says you may not hold water in front of your animal. You may only pour it into a trough. If that case is forbidden, the משנה could not be talking about it.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: And when he holds the bucket
but does not hold it (the cow), is it permitted?
But wasn't it taught:
A person may not fill water
and place it before his animal on Shabbat,
but he may fill and pour it out,
and it drinks on its own!
phrases.notes: The animal drinks from the trough by itself. The person does not hold the water for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי נָקֵיט מָנָא וְלָא נָקֵיט לַהּ, מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case that Step 5 used to reject the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 5's claim that holding the bucket without holding the cow is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids holding water in front of an animal. So the משנה cannot be talking about that case, and the proof from Step 4 seems to come back.

steps.title: אביי limits the ברייתא to a special manger case
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא is talking about a manger standing in the רשות הרבים. It is ten טפחים high and four wide, and one end reaches in between the פסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it already said about this ברייתא: אביי said, here we are dealing with a manger that stands in the רשות הרבים. It is ten טפחים high and four wide, and one end of it goes in between the boards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by quoting אביי. He says the ברייתא is about one unusual setup, not about every case. The next step will explain why that setup is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's ban does not apply to giving an animal water in general. It applies only when the manger sits in the רשות הרבים and only one end reaches inside the enclosure. So in a normal case, holding the bucket alone can still be permitted, and Step 5 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: the upright boards around a well that turn the area into a private domain

phrases.english: Wasn't it already stated about it:
Abaye said,
here it is about a manger standing in the public domain
ten handbreadths high and four wide,
phrases.notes: These measurements make the manger itself count as a רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: and one end of it goes in between the boards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by narrowing the ברייתא to one specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids holding water in front of an animal in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids it only when the manger stands in the רשות הרבים with one end inside the פסין.

steps.title: The reason: a fear he will carry the bucket out
steps.stepSummary: The ban is a rabbinic גזירה. The worry is that he will see the manger is damaged, go to fix it, take the bucket with him, and carry it from the רשות היחיד into the רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a גזירה. He might see that the manger is damaged and go to fix it. He would take the bucket along with him, and so he would carry it from the רשות היחיד to the רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's answer by giving the reason for the ban in that manger case. This is a rabbinic safeguard, not a Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because part of the manger is outside in the רשות הרבים, a person holding the bucket might walk out to fix a damaged spot while still holding it. If he pours the water into the manger instead, the bucket is not in his hand, so this risk does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's ban on holding water in front of an animal applies only to the manger case. It is a גזירה in case he carries the bucket out. Holding the bucket alone in a normal case is not forbidden by it.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest
he sees that the manger is damaged
and comes to fix it,
and carries the bucket along with him,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מַפֵּיק מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.
phrases.english: and so takes it out from the private domain to the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵרָה דִּילְמָא חָזֵי לֵיהּ לְאֵבוּס דִּמְקַלְקַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by explaining why the manger case is forbidden.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the reason for the limited case
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban exists only because of the special risk of carrying the bucket out to the manger in the רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Would he even be liable for carrying the bucket out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the גזירה. רבי יוחנן rules that someone who picks up objects to move them within the house, then changes his mind and carries them out, is פטור, because the first lifting was not for carrying out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in a case like this, would he even be liable? Didn't רב ספרא say in the name of רבי אמי, in the name of רבי יוחנן: Someone who moves his things from corner to corner, then changes his mind about them and carries them out, is פטור, because the first lifting was not done for that purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions אביי's גזירה. Even if the person did carry the bucket out, it seems he would not be liable, so why make a גזירה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for carrying requires an עקירה (lifting) made for the purpose of carrying out. Here, the person lifted the bucket only to water the animal. He decided to go out only later, which matches רבי יוחנן's case of someone who is פטור. So the worry behind the גזירה seems to be about an act that carries no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: one who moves or clears things
lifting an object, the first stage of the מלאכה of carrying

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here does not mean the act is permitted. It means there is no Torah-level liability, because the lifting was not done with the intent to carry out.

phrases.english: And in a case like this, is he liable?
But didn't Rav Safra say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who moves his objects from corner to corner,
and changed his mind about them and carried them out —
is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה עֲקִירָה מִשָּׁעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה לְכָךְ.
phrases.english: because the lifting at the first moment was not for this purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי מִיחַיַּיב? וְהָאָמַר רַב סָפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason for the גזירה given in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's גזירה that he might carry the bucket out to the רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bucket was lifted for watering, not for carrying out. By רבי יוחנן's rule there would be no liability, so the גזירה seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A new reason for the decree: carrying the bucket back in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the old worry and gives a new one. After fixing the manger, he will bring the bucket back in from the רשות הרבים to the רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the worry is this: sometimes he fixes the manger and then brings the bucket back in. Then he is carrying from the public domain into the private domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from רבי יוחנן by changing the reason behind the rabbinic גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי יוחנן's rule, carrying the bucket OUT is only פטור, because when he first picked it up inside, he did not plan to carry it out. So the גמרא moves the worry to the trip back IN. When he picks up the bucket in the רשות הרבים to bring it home, his plan from the start is to carry it into the רשות היחיד, so this would be a full מלאכה. That is a real reason for the גזירה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying carrying out is now allowed. It only says the earlier worry could not justify a גזירה, because by רבי יוחנן's rule that act is only פטור. The new worry is the trip back in, where the plan to carry was there from the start.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because this answer works, the ברייתא no longer disproves Step 5. The משנה can still be read as a case where he holds the bucket but not the cow.

phrases.english: Rather: sometimes he fixes it (the manger)
phrases.notes: אלא signals that the earlier reason is being replaced.

phrases.english: and then brings it (the bucket) back in,
and so he is carrying from the public domain
phrases.notes: Here the lifting is planned from the start for carrying in.

phrases.english: into the private domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: זִמְנִין דִּמְתַקֵּן לֵיהּ וַהֲדַר מְעַיֵּיל לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by replacing the reason given in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the reason behind the rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה is because he might carry the bucket out to fix the manger, but רבי יוחנן says that act is only פטור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה is because he might bring the bucket back in from the רשות הרבים, and that lifting was meant for carrying from the start.

steps.title: Second version: is head-and-most enough for a cow?
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the earlier discussion. For a person, ראשו ורובו is enough. Is it also enough for a cow?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the discussion went like this: for a person, we said it is enough if his head and most of his body are inside. For a cow, is it enough if its head and most of its body are inside, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא retells the earlier discussion in a different version. This time it is framed as an open question about a cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know a person may drink from a domain if his head and most of his body are inside it. The question is whether that is enough for a cow, or whether its whole body must be inside. The first version asked whether ראשה ורובה is required (בעינן); this version asks whether it is enough (סגי), so the easy case and the doubtful case are switched.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (another version of the discussion)
His head and most of his body

steps.confusionAlert: איכא דאמרי does not start a new topic. It retells the same discussion about the cow and the bucket in another form.

phrases.english: Some say:
regarding a person, we already said
that it is enough for him with his head and most of his body (inside).
Regarding a cow, is it enough for it
with its head and most of its body, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: גַּבֵּי אָדָם הָא קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the discussion that the earlier steps of the סוגיא covered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a cow drinking across domains need only its head and most of its body inside, like a person?

steps.title: Narrowing the question to holding only the bucket
steps.stepSummary: If he holds both the bucket and the cow, head-and-most is surely enough. The real question is when he holds only the bucket.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he holds the bucket and holds the cow, don't ask. Head and most is surely enough. Your question is where he holds the bucket but not the cow. What is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the question so we know exactly which case is in doubt. This sets up the proof attempt in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he holds the cow, he can keep it from walking out, so head-and-most is clearly enough. If he holds only the bucket, the cow might wander into the other domain, so maybe more is needed. Only this second case is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't ask about this case (it is obvious)

phrases.english: Where he holds the vessel and holds it (the cow) —
you should not ask
since it is enough with its head and most of its body;
rather, where you should ask

phrases.aramaic: דְּנָקֵיט מָנָא וְלָא נָקֵיט לַהּ, מַאי?
phrases.english: is where he holds the vessel but does not hold it (the cow). What is the rule?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּנָקֵיט מָנָא וְנָקֵיט לַהּ לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question of Step 11 to one specific case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is head-and-most enough for a cow when he holds only the bucket and not the cow?

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about a cow at the well
steps.stepSummary: The משנה requires space for a cow with ראשה ורובה inside to drink. The proof assumes the משנה covers even the case where he holds only the bucket.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: you already learned it: 'as long as a cow can have its head and most of its body inside and drink.' Isn't this speaking of where he holds the bucket but not the cow?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone tries to answer the question using our משנה about the boards around a well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives no detail about holding the cow. So the proof assumes it covers every case, even where he holds only the bucket. If so, head-and-most is enough even then.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a source)
Is it not? (introduces a proposed reading)

phrases.english: He said to him: you already learned it:
"provided that a cow can be
with its head and most of its body inside, and drink."
Is it not speaking where he holds the vessel
and does not hold it (the cow)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of Step 12 from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Head-and-most is enough for a cow even when he holds only the bucket.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁתְּהֵא פָּרָה רֹאשָׁהּ וְרוּבָּהּ מִבִּפְנִים וְשׁוֹתָה

steps.title: The proof is pushed off: he holds the cow too
steps.stepSummary: The משנה may be speaking only where he holds both the bucket and the cow, so it proves nothing about the doubtful case.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is speaking where he holds the vessel and also holds the cow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by limiting the משנה to the easy case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 already said the case where he holds the cow is obvious. If the משנה means that case, it tells us nothing about holding only the bucket. So the question stays unanswered.
steps.whatToRemember: The two versions read the משנה in opposite ways. In the first version (step 5), it is read as a case where he holds only the bucket. In this version, it is read as a case where he holds both the bucket and the cow. Either way, the משנה settles only the case each version considers obvious, so we have no proof that head-and-most is enough for a cow when he holds only the bucket.

phrases.english: No, it is where he holds the vessel and holds it (the cow).
phrases.notes: The reverse of the rejection in Step 5. There the משנה was read as a case where he holds only the bucket; here it is read as a case where he holds the cow too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only. The question itself is left open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה covers holding only the bucket. It may be speaking only where he holds the cow too, which is the obvious case.

steps.title: Support from a teaching that forbids holding only the bucket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the idea that the משנה speaks only where he holds both. It cites a ברייתא that forbids filling water and holding it before one's animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense this way. If he holds only the bucket and not the cow, is that allowed at all? A ברייתא teaches: a person may not fill water and put it in front of his animal. But he may fill it and pour it out, and the animal drinks on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer it just gave in step 14. Holding only the bucket is forbidden anyway, so the משנה must be talking about holding both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the משנה may speak only where he holds both the bucket and the cow. This ברייתא seems to show that holding only the bucket is forbidden. If so, the משנה could never be talking about that case, so it gives no answer about ראשה ורובה when he holds only the bucket.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too it is logical (introduces support)
But it was taught in a ברייתא
Fills and pours out (into a trough)

phrases.english: And so too it is reasonable,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי נָקֵיט מָנָא וְלָא נָקֵיט לַהּ,
phrases.english: for if he holds the bucket but does not hold it (the cow),
is it permitted?
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
A person may not fill water
and place it before his animal,
but he may fill and pour out
and it drinks on its own!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the דחיה of step 14 by showing that holding only the bucket is forbidden anyway.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה speaks only where he holds both the bucket and the cow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding one to fill water and set it before his animal, while permitting pouring into a trough.

steps.title: אביי explains the teaching as a special case of a manger
steps.stepSummary: The support is rejected. אביי already explained that the ברייתא speaks of a manger in the רשות הרבים whose end reaches between the פסין, where the רבנן decreed out of concern that he will carry the bucket out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it already said about this ברייתא, in the name of אביי: Here we are dealing with a manger standing in the רשות הרבים. It is ten טפחים high and four wide, and its end goes in between the פסין. The concern is that sometimes he will see the manger is damaged and go to fix it. He will take the bucket with him and carry it from the רשות היחיד to the רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the support from step 15. That ברייתא is not a general rule against holding only the bucket. It is a special decree for one unusual setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי limits the ברייתא to a manger that is itself a רשות היחיד, sitting in the רשות הרבים with one end inside the פסין. The ban comes from a worry that he will walk out with the bucket to fix the manger. So the ברייתא says nothing about the ordinary case in the משנה, and the support is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it already stated about it
The upright boards placed around a well to make an enclosure

steps.confusionAlert: This explanation of אביי appeared earlier on the דף in the first version. The גמרא is really repeating it here for a new purpose: to knock down the support brought in step 15.

phrases.english: Wasn't it stated regarding it
that Abaye said:
Here it deals with a manger standing in the public domain
ten handbreadths high and four wide,
phrases.notes: These measurements make the manger itself a private domain.

phrases.english: and its end enters between the boards,
for at times he sees that the manger is damaged
and comes to fix it,
and carries the bucket with him,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מַפֵּיק מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.
phrases.english: and so carries out from the private domain to the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support of step 15 by limiting the ברייתא to a special manger case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not decide the original question about ראשה ורובה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא is a general ban. In fact it is a special decree tied to a manger reaching into the רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Would he really be liable for carrying out after changing his mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's reason using רבי יוחנן's rule. Someone who lifts an object for a permitted purpose and then decides to carry it out is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a case like this, would he even be liable? But רב ספרא said in the name of רבי אמי, in the name of רבי יוחנן: One who moves his things from corner to corner in his house, then changes his mind and takes them out, is פטור. This is because when he first lifted them, it was not for that purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's reason for the decree. Carrying the bucket out in that way would not even be a real Torah violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he lifted the bucket, he meant only to water the animal. He decided to go out only later. According to רבי יוחנן, the lifting (עקירה) must be done for the purpose of carrying out. Without that he is פטור, so there seems to be no reason to make a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: One who clears or moves things
Lifting an object up from its place, the start of carrying

phrases.english: But in such a case, is he liable?
But didn't Rav Safra say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
One who moves his objects from corner to corner
and changed his mind about them and took them out
is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה עֲקִירָה מִשָּׁעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה לְכָךְ!
phrases.english: because the lifting at the first moment was not for this purpose!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason אביי gave in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's concern that he will carry the bucket out to the רשות הרבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bucket was first lifted for a different purpose. Under רבי יוחנן's rule, carrying it out after a change of mind is פטור, so a decree based on this worry makes no sense.

steps.title: The worry is bringing the bucket back in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reason for the decree. After fixing the manger, he may lift the bucket in the רשות הרבים and bring it back into the רשות היחיד, which is a full violation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: sometimes he fixes the manger and then brings the bucket back in. He then carries it from the רשות הרבים into the רשות היחיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by swapping in a new worry. The decree stands, so the ברייתא is still a special case and the support from step 15 still fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he picks up the bucket in the רשות הרבים to go back, he lifts it intending to bring it into the רשות היחיד. That is a proper עקירה for carrying, so רבי יוחנן's exemption does not apply. The ברייתא is still a special decree about the manger, so it cannot prove that holding only the bucket is forbidden in general.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that forbids holding a bucket before one's animal is a special decree about a manger reaching into the רשות הרבים. The worry is that he will carry the bucket back in. So it cannot be used to show that the משנה speaks only where he holds both the bucket and the cow.

phrases.english: Rather:
at times he fixes it
and then brings it back in,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מְעַיֵּיל לֵיהּ מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד.
phrases.english: and so carries it in from the public domain to the private domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 by replacing the reason for אביי's decree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reason behind the decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree was out of concern that he would carry the bucket out to fix the manger.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree is out of concern that he will bring the bucket back in from the רשות הרבים, with a proper עקירה for that purpose.

steps.title: A proof from force-feeding a camel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a camel may be force-fed from inside only if its head and most of its body are inside. Force-feeding means holding both the bucket and the animal, yet head and most of the body are still required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a camel whose head and most of its body are inside may be force-fed from inside. But force-feeding is like holding the bucket and also holding the animal, and still we require its head and most of its body to be inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the idea that holding both the bucket and the animal makes it permitted. This ברייתא shows that even in such a case, more is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you force-feed (אבוס) an animal, you must grab its neck while holding the food, so you are holding both. Even so, the ברייתא requires the camel's head and most of its body to be inside. That suggests holding both is not enough by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. Introduces a source brought as a proof or a challenge.
Its head and most of its body
Force-feed; stuff food into the animal's mouth

steps.confusionAlert: Force-feeding (אבוס) is not the same as ordinary feeding. The whole point here is that force-feeding automatically means you are holding the animal too.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A camel whose head and most of its body are inside
may be force-fed from inside,
but force-feeding is like one who holds the bucket
phrases.notes: You cannot force-feed without holding the food.

phrases.english: and also holds the animal,
phrases.notes: You must grip the animal's neck to force-feed it.

phrases.english: and still we require its head and most of its body to be inside!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: גָּמָל שֶׁרֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ מִבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא about the manger was explained away, the גמרא brings a new source about force-feeding.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that holding both the bucket and the animal is enough to permit feeding.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Force-feeding always involves holding both, yet the ברייתא still requires head and most of the body inside. So holding both does not suffice.

steps.title: A camel is different because of its long neck
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that a camel is a special case. Its long neck lets it stretch into the outer domain, so extra stringency applies only to camels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב הונא said in the name of רב ששת: a camel is different, since its neck is long.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא to camels only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A camel's long neck can reach far into the רשות הרבים, so the feeder might follow it there with the bucket. That is why חכמים required its head and most of its body inside. For an ordinary animal held along with the bucket, there may be no such concern.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. Used to set a case apart from the general rule.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Huna said
that Rav Sheshet said:
A camel is different,
since its neck is long.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the camel ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the ruling is limited to camels for a reason unique to them.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that every animal needs head and most of its body inside, even when held.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a camel needs this, because its long neck creates a special risk. Other animals that are held may not need it.

steps.title: A second proof about any animal
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא states the same rule about any בהמה, not just a camel. So the long-neck answer would not work here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: an animal whose head and most of its body are inside may be force-fed from inside. But force-feeding is like holding the bucket and also holding the animal, and still we require its head and most of its body to be inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that uses the general word 'בהמה' (animal). This renews the same challenge without the camel exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is exactly the same as before: force-feeding means holding both, yet head and most of the body are required. The only change is that this source speaks about any animal, so רב ששת's answer about a camel's long neck seems not to help.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal (general term, such as a cow)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An animal whose head and most of its body are inside
may be force-fed from inside.
But force-feeding is like one who holds the bucket
and also holds the animal,
and still we require its head and most of its body to be inside!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁרֹאשָׁהּ וְרוּבָּהּ בִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same challenge with a source about animals in general, sidestepping the camel answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that holding both is enough, and רב ששת's answer limiting the rule to camels.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even an ordinary animal needs head and most of its body inside during force-feeding, then holding both is not enough, and the camel exception does not explain the ruling.

steps.title: The word 'animal' here also means a camel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'בהמה' in this ברייתא is also a camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'animal' that it teaches? It is also a camel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge by reading the general word 'בהמה' as referring specifically to a camel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'בהמה' here means a camel, then רב ששת's long-neck reason applies again. The ברייתא would then say nothing about ordinary animals.

phrases.english: What is the 'animal' that it teaches? It is also
a camel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by bringing the second ברייתא back under רב ששת's camel exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בהמה' means any animal, so the rule applies even to ordinary animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בהמה' here means a camel, so the long-neck reason still explains the ruling.

steps.title: One source says animal and another says camel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: there is a ברייתא that says 'בהמה' and a separate one that says 'גמל'. So 'בהמה' must mean something wider than a camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught 'animal', and it was taught 'camel'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the previous answer by pointing out that two different ברייתות use two different words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'בהמה' simply meant a camel, there would be no reason for one source to say 'בהמה' and another to say 'גמל'. The different wording shows that the rule covers ordinary animals too. That would bring back the proof that ראשה ורובה is required even when he holds both the bucket and the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא. Introduces a source used to object.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new case. The objection rests only on the fact that the two ברייתות use different words, which shows they mean different things.

phrases.english: But it was taught 'animal'
and it was taught 'camel'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 22 that 'בהמה' means a camel.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'בהמה' in the ברייתא means a camel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separate ברייתות say 'בהמה' and 'גמל'. The different wording shows 'בהמה' includes other animals, so the camel exception cannot explain the rule.

steps.title: The two ברייתות were not taught side by side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 23. The ברייתא that says 'בהמה' and the one that says 'גמל' come from different places, so different wording proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Were these two ברייתות taught next to each other?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 23. It says the two ברייתות were not taught together, so one of them could have used the word 'בהמה' to mean a camel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 argued that a ברייתא saying 'בהמה' and another saying 'גמל' must mean different things. The answer is that if one תנא had taught both together, he would not switch words for the same case. But these ברייתות come from different sources, so one תנא could easily call a camel 'בהמה'. That keeps רב ששת's 'camel only' answer standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it? Were they? (opens a rhetorical question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is a rhetorical question that answers the challenge: 'They were not taught together, so the different wording proves nothing.'

phrases.english: Were they taught next to each other?!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical. Since the ברייתות are separate, different wording does not mean different cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 23 by removing its assumption that both ברייתות share one style of wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different sources may use different wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because two ברייתות used different words ('בהמה' and 'גמל'), they must be talking about different animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות were taught separately. One תנא could call a camel 'בהמה', so both can be talking about a camel.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the idea that a camel is special
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אלעזר: he forbids this with a camel because its neck is long. This supports רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: רבי אלעזר forbids it with a camel, since its neck is long.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב ששת. In it, רבי אלעזר is strict with a camel for exactly the reason רב ששת gave: its long neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said in Step 20 that the 'head and most of the body' rule is special to camels because of their long necks. Here a תנא, רבי אלעזר, says the same thing. This shows that a camel really does have its own stricter rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (introduces a supporting ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: A camel's long neck can stretch out of the permitted area. That is why a camel needs its head and most of its body inside, while other animals have a more lenient rule.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Elazar forbids it with a camel,
since its neck is long.
phrases.notes: The same reason רב ששת gave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the challenge, the גמרא brings positive support for רב ששת.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's claim that the stricter rule applies only to a camel because of its long neck
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אלעזר, who is strict with a camel because its neck is long

steps.title: פסי ביראות were permitted only for festival pilgrims
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אדא says the leniency of פסי ביראות was made only for עולי רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אדא said: Boards around wells were permitted only for festival pilgrims.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רבי יצחק בר אדא limits who the leniency of פסי ביראות was made for: only עולי רגלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסי ביראות are boards set around a well. They make a loose enclosure so people can draw water on שבת. רבי יצחק בר אדא says this leniency was not made for everyone. It was made for the many pilgrims traveling to ירושלים, who needed water on the way.

keyTerms.meaning: Boards placed around wells to form a partial enclosure
Festival pilgrims going up to ירושלים

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that פסי ביראות are a special leniency made for a specific need, not a normal רשות היחיד for everyone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Adda said:
Boards around wells were not permitted
except for festival pilgrims alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: who the leniency of פסי ביראות was made for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency of פסי ביראות applies only to עולי רגלים.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the leniency was only for animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says פסי ביראות were permitted only for animals, which seems to contradict רבי יצחק בר אדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: Boards around wells were permitted only for animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק בר אדא with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says the leniency was made only for animals, not for pilgrims.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק בר אדא limited the leniency by who is using it: pilgrims. The ברייתא seems to limit it in another way: animals only. These look like two different rules, so the ברייתא seems to argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught? (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
For animals, for the needs of an animal

phrases.english: But it was taught: Boards around wells were not permitted
except for animals alone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement of Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק בר אדא's rule that פסי ביראות are only for עולי רגלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits the leniency to animals, not to pilgrims, so it seems to contradict him.

steps.title: It means the animals of festival pilgrims
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'animals' in the ברייתא means the animals of עולי רגלים. Then it begins to explain what the rule is for a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'animal'? The animals of festival pilgrims. But a person…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources agree. The ברייתא's 'animal' means the animals of pilgrims. Then 'אבל אדם' sets up the next point, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combining the two sources gives one rule: the leniency is for the animals of עולי רגלים. So there is no argument. The words 'אבל אדם' start to explain how a person's case is different from an animal's.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (asks for the meaning of a word)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אבל אדם' is not finished here. The rule about a person continues in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: What is 'animal'?
The animals of festival pilgrims.
But a person
phrases.notes: Sets up the next statement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27 by reading the two sources together.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says 'animals' instead of pilgrims, so it argues with רבי יצחק בר אדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Animals' means the animals of עולי רגלים, so both sources agree.
